story.headline: DeepSeek Nears Massive Funding Round Backed by Major Strategic Investors
story.summary: DeepSeek is finalizing a major funding round expected to surpass $11 billion, backed by major stakeholders like Tencent and CATL to finance compute infrastructure. The company continues to accelerate its model rollouts as release intervals shrink across Chinese AI developers.

draft.body:
Chinese artificial intelligence developer DeepSeek is finalizing an expanded fundraising effort that could reach up to 100 billion yuan ($14.9 billion), according to reporting on October 6, 2026. As reported by [Bloomberg via TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/deepseek-12bn-funding-round-tencent-catl), the company is close to securing at least 80 billion yuan ($12 billion) in capital. DeepSeek originally targeted 50 billion yuan, but swelling investor interest following the release of its latest flagship model prompted the company to expand the round. The influx of private and state-backed capital positions the startup for heavy infrastructure expansion and a planned initial public offering in early 2027.

DeepSeek is seeking a valuation of roughly 500 billion yuan ($74 billion to $75 billion) in the current talks, as reported by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/deepseek-funding-round.html). The transaction marks the laboratory's second external capital raise, following a maiden outside round completed in June 2026 that netted approximately 50 billion yuan at an implied valuation of 350 billion yuan.

[[FIG1]]

## Strategic Backers in the DeepSeek Funding Round

Tencent and battery manufacturer Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL) are committing some of the largest sums to the current round, according to [Bloomberg reporting on Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/deepseek-set-to-raise-at-least-12-bln-in-tencent-catlled-round-bloomberg-4933370). They are joined by automotive manufacturer Geely Auto, Monolith Management, Loyal Valley Capital, and government-backed investment funds.

Both Tencent and CATL were anchor participants in DeepSeek's initial June financing. In that earlier round, DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng provided 20 billion yuan of his own capital, while Tencent contributed 10 billion yuan and CATL added 5 billion yuan, alongside NetEase, JD.com, and China's national AI investment fund, according to [TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/deepseek-12bn-funding-round-tencent-catl).

DeepSeek has strictly controlled its investor registry during the recent process. Sources told [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/deepseek-funding-round.html) that the company vetted prospective backers closely, excluding retail-backed private equity funds to focus on corporate partners and state-backed institutions. The funding process took longer than an initial August deadline because some prospective participants negotiated terms over the $75 billion valuation.

The investment aligns with concrete commercial deployments. Tencent previously integrated DeepSeek's models into products including WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy, according to [xenospectrum.com](https://xenospectrum.com/en/deepseek-funding-low-cost-ai-infrastructure/), while expanding its own compute access abroad, as reported by [qz.com](https://qz.com/deepseek-funding-round-tencent-catl-ipo-100626). For CATL, which highlighted data center energy management and battery storage systems in its 2025 sustainability reporting, the tie-up offers closer alignment with major compute operations, according to [xenospectrum.com](https://xenospectrum.com/en/deepseek-funding-low-cost-ai-infrastructure/).

[[FIG2]]

## Compute Infrastructure and Domestic Hardware Expansion

A substantial share of the newly secured funds is earmarked for domestic data center infrastructure. According to reporting compiled by [qz.com](https://qz.com/deepseek-funding-round-tencent-catl-ipo-100626), DeepSeek is constructing a large-scale data center facility in Inner Mongolia. The site is designed to host a minimum of 160,000 high-end accelerators from Huawei Technologies, representing one of the largest planned concentrations of domestic Chinese AI hardware.

To bridge the gap between foreign and domestic silicon, DeepSeek has rolled out specialized developer tools. On September 30, 2026, the company updated its "TileKernels" compute library to support Huawei's Ascend architecture alongside Nvidia GPUs, enabling both chip types to be programmed via a unified Python interface, as detailed by [xenospectrum.com](https://xenospectrum.com/en/deepseek-funding-low-cost-ai-infrastructure/). DeepSeek also published "DeepGEMM-Ascend," an open matrix-operation library specifically validated for Huawei's Ascend 950 processor.

Fund negotiations paused earlier this year after remarks from founder Liang Wenfeng surfaced regarding the domestic industry's persistent lag behind American AI capabilities and its heavy reliance on Nvidia hardware, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/deepseek-funding-round.html). Despite the friction, Liang has reiterated commitments to prioritize advancing artificial general intelligence over commercial profitability while keeping weights openly accessible.

## Model Architecture, Efficiency Gains, and API Pricing

The funding surge arrived on the heels of DeepSeek's September 10 release of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The model uses networks of different parameter sizes optimized for processing long input contexts and generating shorter responses, such as agentic document processing and code analysis, according to documentation analyzed by [xenospectrum.com](https://xenospectrum.com/en/deepseek-funding-low-cost-ai-infrastructure/).

According to the official model card, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash expands the core model to 552 billion parameters, compared to 284 billion in the prior V4-Flash. However, active per-token parameters during input context processing dropped from 13 billion to 8 billion, while output generation routes through 16 billion active parameters.

In addition to parameter decoupling, DeepSeek redesigned key-value cache handling across layers. The company states that V4.1-Flash reduces high-bandwidth memory capacity requirements for the KV cache to one-quarter of the earlier architecture, while cutting required SSD storage for caching to one-eighth.

The resulting operational efficiencies are reflected in DeepSeek's public API structure. For input tokens utilizing cache reuse, pricing is set at $0.003 per million tokens during off-peak hours (all day on weekends and Chinese holidays) and $0.006 per million tokens during peak weekday windows. Input without cache reuse costs $0.15 off-peak and $0.30 during peak hours. Output tokens are billed at $0.60 per million tokens off-peak and $1.20 during peak periods. The base model weights remain distributed under the MIT license.

## Road to an Early 2027 STAR Market Listing

Once the funding round formally concludes in October, DeepSeek plans to initiate corporate restructuring to prepare for an initial public offering in early 2027, as reported by [qz.com](https://qz.com/deepseek-funding-round-tencent-catl-ipo-100626). The company has retained CITIC Securities to structure a potential listing on the Shanghai Stock Exchange Science and Technology Innovation Board, known as the STAR Market.

DeepSeek is not alone in expediting public listing schedules. Rival developer Moonshot AI is also targeting an early 2027 public listing after securing investment at a $50 billion valuation, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/deepseek-funding-round.html).

These market moves coincide with rapid deployment timelines across the sector. A study reported by [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/deepseek-xiaomi-ship-16-ai-models-in-a-month-as-us-labs-urge-pacing) revealed that the average development interval across leading US and Chinese AI labs compressed from 125 days down to 44 days between April and September 2026. Chinese developers shipped 16 models in September alone, with DeepSeek carrying out monthly updates since July, Alibaba and Z.AI releasing models successively after August, and Xiaomi releasing in September.
